title: Fog vs Cloud vs Edge Comparisons — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public fog data science knowledge, fact-checked reference. Fog, cloud, and edge compared side by side: latency, cost, capacity, and when each wins. Fog, edge, and cloud are complementary tiers, not rivals. Cloud offers effectively unlimited, elastic compute and global reach at 50-150 ms away. Edge computing pushes work onto the device itself or its immediate gateway (lowest latency, tightest resources). Fog sits between: a multi-tier, network-integrated layer with more capacity than edge devices and far lower latency than cloud, spanning many nodes. The discipline is choosing per workload: train in the cloud, infer at the fog, sense at the edge — and revisiting the choice as workloads and networks evolve.
